title: IDTA Submodel Templates for the Asset Administration Shell
usedFor: Candidate semanticIds for our AAS submodel templates. IDTA publishes an official 7-part Digital Battery Passport family — the most on-point sectoral match this register has found for the current battery focus.
licence: CC-BY-4.0, confirmed 2026-08-11 two ways: `gh api repos/admin-shell-io/submodel-templates` reports `license.spdx_id: "CC-BY-4.0"`, and the repo-root `LICENSE.txt`, fetched and read directly, is genuine CC BY 4.0 legal text. The grant is at repo level, covering the whole `published/` tree of PDFs, JSON and AASX together — individual spec PDFs (checked IDTA-02035-4) carry no separate inline copyright text.
source: https://github.com/admin-shell-io/submodel-templates, `published/Digital Battery Passport/` (IDTA-02035-1 through -7, v1.0, Feb 2026) — fetched and read directly, cross-checked against `crates/dpp-aas/src/sectors/battery.rs`.
finding: **Correction to the prior record**: IDTA-02011 is "Hierarchical Structures enabling Bills of Material", not "Generic Frame for Technical Data for Industrial Equipment in Manufacturing" as previously recorded — that title belongs to **IDTA-02003** instead (confirmed by the repo's own folder naming and by Digital Battery Passport Part 4's `administration.templateId: "IDTA-02003-2-0"`). The prior record's substantive point survives (a generic technical-data frame isn't a physical-properties template), only the document number was wrong — worth catching before it propagated, the same defect class the 2026-07-29 removals existed to stop. **New finding — IDTA-02035, Digital Battery Passport, 7 parts, explicitly aligned to DIN DKE SPEC 99100 and the Battery Regulation**: Part 3 (Carbon Footprint) reuses IDTA-02023's identifier unchanged (a battery *profile* of the generic template, not a distinct one); Part 4 (Technical Data) is `https://admin-shell.io/idta/digitalbatterypassport/TechnicalData/1/0`; Part 6 (Material Composition) is a SAMM URN, `urn:samm:io.admin-shell.idta.batterypass.material_composition:1.0.0#MaterialComposition` — same family as `batterypass-samm`/Catena-X, not a plain `admin-shell.io` path. Field comparison against `battery.rs`'s submodel: direct correspondence on `nominalVoltageV`, `nominalCapacityAh`, `expectedLifetimeCycles`, `batteryWeightKg`, `co2ePerUnitKg`, `carbonFootprintClass` (six fields, ready to map). Same concept at finer IDTA granularity: round-trip efficiency (1 field here vs. IDTA's initial/50%-cycle-life/fade split), internal resistance (1 vs. IDTA's initial/increase × cell/pack/module), operating temperature (2 vs. idle-state plus charging-state boundaries). **The recycled-content gap is now confirmed by a third independent source**: IDTA Part 7's `RecycledContentInformation` uses the same pre-/post-consumer split `batterypass-samm` already flagged — our flat per-metal percentages are the outlier across three unrelated organisations' models, not any one vocabulary's quirk. Not found anywhere checked: an equivalent to `stateOfHealthPct`/`sohMethodology`, `dueDiligenceUrl` (Handover Documentation is a generic VDI2770 document container, no dedicated field), or CRM country-of-origin (Part 6 flags `IsCriticalRawMaterial` but has no origin-country property). Parts 1 and 2 not yet checked against `gtin`/`batteryType`/`batteryChemistry`.
nextStep: Map the six direct-correspondence fields as semanticIds now that the licence is confirmed. Treat the recycled-content pre-/post-consumer split as a confirmed gap independent of any IRI decision — three unrelated sources now agree, prioritise its Annex II/XIII citation. Decide, as a data-model question not a semanticId swap, whether to adopt IDTA's finer resistance/efficiency splits. Verify Parts 1-2 against `gtin`/`batteryType`/`batteryChemistry` before closing this out fully.
